cohort: The study included 64 infants diagnosed with laryngomalacia (mean age 4.6 months) and a control group of 64 healthy infants (mean age 4.5 months).
finding: Infants with laryngomalacia had statistically significantly lower vitamin D levels and different PTH levels compared to healthy controls, with severe laryngomalacia associated with even lower vitamin D levels.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for infants at a mean age of approximately 4.5-4.6 months.
